title: ReguLens benchmark question
description: One evaluation item. The gradeable ground truth is required_evidence - the set of document sections that must be retrieved for the question to be answerable. answer_sketch is a human aid, not a scored field.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. Q001. Never reuse an id after retiring a question.

question.description: The question as a user would ask it. Avoid quoting the regulation verbatim - that turns the task into string matching.

category.description: unanswerable items have an empty required_evidence list and test whether the system abstains instead of confabulating.

required_evidence.description: Every section that MUST be retrieved. Recall is measured against this set. Keep it minimal - include only sections without which the question cannot be answered.

doc_id.description: Must match a doc_id in corpus/registry.csv.

section.description: Section or article identifier as printed in the document, e.g. 'Article 5' or '6.1.6'.

why.description: One line on what this section contributes. Forces you to justify each label.

helpful_evidence.description: Sections that add useful context but are not strictly required. Not scored for recall; used to check whether extra retrievals are relevant or noise.

answer_sketch.description: Your own plain-language note on what the evidence says. NOT scored, NOT a legal opinion, and never presented as one.

source.description: Be honest here. If an LLM drafted it, say so - and it still requires human verification of required_evidence before it counts.

minutes_to_label.description: How long it took to establish the evidence set by hand. Useful signal: items taking over ~20 minutes are probably too ambiguous to label reliably.

confidence.description: Your confidence that required_evidence is complete and correct. Report the distribution in the README; consider excluding low-confidence items from headline metrics.

retired.description: Set true instead of deleting, so results stay reproducible across runs.
